lines.title: Advice and asset management under the new regimes
lines.md:
A bank can advise clients on virtual assets (VAs) and manage funds or client accounts that hold them, for a fee. (concept)

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Adviser; discretionary portfolio manager; fund manager |
| Client segments | Private banking, retail, institutional |
| Value chain | Advise and manage |
| Regulatory gate | Today: registration with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for advice or asset management, plus SFC terms for VA (virtual asset) work. Next: registration under new VA advisory and management regimes [S:8a016a912528, para 26; S:40148cf96f41, Part I, p.3; S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Conclusions published [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 64, 67] |
| Related modules | [C1](#m-C1), [C2](#m-C2), [B1](#m-B1), [E1](#m-E1) |
| Related cases | [Case 5: The board's strategic plan](#case-5-board-strategic-plan) |
## What the bank does

- Intermediaries, including banks, should give VA advice only to clients of their securities dealing (Type 1) or securities advice (Type 4) business. [S:8a016a912528, para 26] This limit does not apply to a bank that advises only on stablecoins licensed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). [S:a0bd48559762, para (7), p.6]
- Before recommending a VA to a retail client, the adviser should check that it is a large, liquid token. [S:8a016a912528, para 28(a)] That means it is in at least two acceptable indices (published lists that track major tokens) from two different index providers. [S:8a016a912528, para 28(a)]
- SFC terms for VA fund managers apply in two cases. A fund states a VA aim, or it plans to hold at least 10% of its total assets in VAs. Total assets here means gross asset value (GAV). [S:40148cf96f41, Part I, de minimis threshold, p.3]
- For retail discretionary accounts (where the manager decides the trades), the manager should trade only large-cap VAs (tokens with a large total market value). [S:40148cf96f41, Schedule 2, para 2] Stablecoins issued by HKMA licensees are exempt from that liquidity test. [S:40148cf96f41, Schedule 2, para 2]
- A registered institution (RI) is a bank registered with the SFC. Holding HKMA-licensed stablecoins, and no other VAs, in the portfolios it manages does not on its own make an RI need an asset management registration. [S:a0bd48559762, para (6), p.5] If a portfolio meets the 10% test above, the SFC's VA manager terms still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, para (6), p.5]
- Under the proposed new regimes, only banks could register with the SFC instead of taking a licence. [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]

## Revenue levers

- A management fee is a yearly charge on the value of assets under management (AUM). (concept)
- A performance fee is a share of gains above an agreed level. (concept)
- An advice fee is paid by the client. A commission or rebate is paid by the product provider, and can create a conflict of interest. (concept)
- For HKMA-licensed stablecoins, a bank should base advice on thorough analysis. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6] It should not use commission rebates as the main reason to recommend one. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- A licensed VA manager that deals in VAs only to run its portfolios would not need a separate VA dealing licence. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 38] For example, it could accept VAs as fund subscriptions and convert them. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 38]

## Cost and capital drivers

- A VA fund manager should place fund assets with a separate, independent custodian and keep them segregated. [S:40148cf96f41, para 4.1] It should disclose plans to keep over 10% of GAV with one custodian or in self-custody. [S:40148cf96f41, para 4.11]
- A VA fund manager should tell the SFC, and the HKMA for an RI, at least 7 business days before any significant business change. [S:40148cf96f41, para 7.2]
- The new VA management regime is to have no small-amount exception. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32] So managing even a small VA portfolio for others would need a licence or registration. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32] Advice on a mixed portfolio of VAs and securities would still need VA advisory licensing or registration for the VA part. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 21]
- Under current SFC fees, an RI pays HK$23,500 to apply and HK$35,000 a year for each of advice and asset management. [S:6186c01c6649, para 67] The May 2026 conclusions tie the new VA fees to those fees. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 59]
- Non-bank licensees holding client assets would need HK$5 million paid-up capital and HK$3 million liquid capital. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 25, 48] Those figures exclude banks. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 25, 48]
- Every RI must appoint at least two executive officers (EOs) to supervise each regulated activity directly. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4]

## Official signals

- Hong Kong's asset and wealth management AUM rose 20% to HK$42,202 billion at end-2025. [S:6d9deb07299d, para 1]
- Assets in private banking and private wealth management rose 24% to HK$12,945 billion at end-2025. [S:6d9deb07299d, para 5] Forty-seven registered institutions (RIs) reported doing that business. [S:6d9deb07299d, para 45]
- The SFC survey cites a study commissioned by Invest Hong Kong, the Government's investment promotion agency. [S:6d9deb07299d, para 30] It counts over 3,380 single-family offices (firms that manage one family's wealth) in Hong Kong at end-2025. [S:6d9deb07299d, para 30] It notes strong interest in digital assets among their alternative investments. [S:6d9deb07299d, para 31]
- The consultation on the VA advisory and management regimes drew 51 responses. [S:4a0342268bf2, Note 2, p.1]
- SFC-licensed firms and registered banks that already give VA advice or management are to get a faster approval process. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 67] The start date is not set yet. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
- The Government and the SFC do not plan to treat existing VA advisers or managers as licensed while they apply. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63] The regimes take full effect on their start date. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63]
- The Government said one bill covering VA dealing, custody, advisory and management would go to the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (3), 'In addition' para]

## Industry benchmarks

- HashKey Holdings Limited (HashKey), a Hong Kong-listed platform group, reported 2025 asset management revenue of HK$117.1 million, up from HK$78.2 million. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.12] It said the rise came mainly from carried interest, a share of fund profits. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.12]
- HashKey's 2025 annual results reported asset management AUM of HK$7.2 billion at end-2025. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.5] These are group figures and include markets outside Hong Kong.
- Bosera Asset Management (International) published a Hong Kong prospectus in March 2026 (reported figures). It sets a current management fee of 0.60% a year for the listed shares of its bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF). [I:d81073907a14, PDF p.96]

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Is VA advice and management a new fee line, or a way to keep private-banking wealth inside the bank?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Fee income is roughly AUM times the fee rate. AUM moves with VA prices, so income moves too.
> - Costs include registration, independent custody, staff with VA skills and extra suitability checks.
> - Once the new regime applies, the VA rules cover even a small VA part of a mixed portfolio.
> - A question to test: do clients who want VA exposure move assets elsewhere when the bank offers none?
> **What it depends on:** client demand; VA prices; the start date; the speed of approval; custody costs.
> **Official signposts:**
> - Faster approval for firms already in the business. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 67]
> - No small-amount exception for VA management. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 32]
> - The bill planned for 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (3), 'In addition' para]
> **What this is not:** not a forecast, not advice and not the regulator's view.

## Read next

- Module [C1 Selling, dealing and advising on virtual assets](#m-C1)
- Module [C2 VA funds and ETFs](#m-C2) (ETFs: exchange-traded funds)
- Module [B1 Your bank's legal status for digital assets](#m-B1)
- Module [E1 What's coming: the pipeline](#m-E1)

- Project profile: [Relevant Stablecoins: dealing, advice and trading](#p-relevant-stablecoins)

lines.title: Banking the digital-asset industry
lines.md:
In this line a bank provides accounts, payments and safekeeping to firms that work with digital assets, such as trading platforms and stablecoin issuers (concept).

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Account bank; client-money bank; reserve bank and custodian; payment provider |
| Client segments | Institutional, fintechs |
| Value chain | Hold, Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | The bank's existing authorisation plus adequate risk controls [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3]. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) expects banks to discuss virtual-asset (VA) plans with it, and get its feedback, before launch [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3] |
| Related modules | [D3](#m-D3), [C7](#m-C7), [C4](#m-C4), [B2](#m-B2) |
| Related cases | [Case 3: The reserve bank that also sells the coin](#case-3-stablecoin-reserve-distributor), [Case 4: The night the hot wallet emptied](#case-4-vatp-incident) |
## What the bank does

- Holds client money for trading platforms. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) expects each licensed VA trading platform (VATP) to keep client money in separate accounts [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.11(a)]. The platform's associated entity (the linked company that holds client assets) should open these accounts [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.11(a)]. They sit with a Hong Kong authorized financial institution, or an overseas bank the SFC agrees to [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.11(a)]. Within one business day, client money received should be paid into such an account or paid out as the client directs [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.11(b)].
- Holds stablecoin reserves. The HKMA expects a licensed stablecoin issuer to appoint qualified custodians for its reserves [S:240be6833157, para 2.5.4]. The issuer should use a licensed bank, or another custodian set-up that the HKMA accepts [S:240be6833157, para 2.5.4]. Reserves may include bank deposits with a term of up to three months [S:240be6833157, para 2.3.1].
- Runs payments for customers who buy virtual assets (VAs). In January 2022 the HKMA said it did not then intend to stop this [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3]. The condition is adequate risk controls with senior management oversight [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3].
- Moves VAs for customers. The HKMA says the anti-money-laundering (AML) law allows this if the transfer rules in section 13A of its Schedule 2 are met [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II, para 4.3].

## Revenue levers

- Account and payment fees are charged per transaction or per month on operating accounts (concept).
- Deposit balances earn the bank net interest margin: the gap between what it earns on the money and what it pays the depositor (concept).
- Reserve custody earns a fee, usually a small yearly share of the assets held (concept).
- Foreign-exchange conversion on payments in and out of platforms adds a spread, the gap between buying and selling rates (concept).

## Cost and capital drivers

- Customer due diligence (CDD): the HKMA expects a risk assessment of each client that is a VA service provider (VASP) [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]. Checks may cover its business model, its licence status and its AML controls [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4].
- Overseas clients: for a VASP outside Hong Kong, the bank should apply its correspondent-banking checks (extra checks used for banks that serve other banks) [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23]. It should find out whether the account serves the VASP itself or the VASP's own customers [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.24]. It could consider asking for separate accounts for the two [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.25].
- Monitoring: the HKMA expects banks to watch for frequent transfers to or from VA platforms [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3-4]. Where there are grounds for suspicion, banks should file a report [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3-4].
- Scam money: the SFC cites police intelligence on scam money moved by bank transfer to licensed firms [S:be46918f8aa2, para 8]. Some is turned into VAs and withdrawn to unhosted wallets (wallets not held by a regulated firm) [S:be46918f8aa2, para 8].
- Direct debits: the SFC has flagged risks in simplified electronic Direct Debit Authorisation (eDDA) set-ups used by licensed firms to collect client deposits [S:cfc4a0d9f1be, para 1].

## Official signals

- The SFC listed 13 licensed trading platforms at its 29 May 2026 update [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; Last update line].
- The HKMA licensed two stablecoin issuers from a first batch of 36 applicants [S:193316443831, Assessment of licence applications, paras 1-2].
- The Government told the Legislative Council in February 2024 that VA-related crime cases rose from 1,397 in 2021 to 3,415 in 2023 [S:4bd22ccf481d, Reply (1)-(2)]. Money involved rose from HK$824 million to HK$4,398 million [S:4bd22ccf481d, Reply (1)-(2)].
- The HKMA warned in November 2024 that some overseas crypto firms called themselves banks without a Hong Kong licence [S:19c8611c621a, paras 1-2].
- The SFC plans to switch on the AML surveillance part of its crypto data initiative (CrypTech) in 2027 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)].
- The Customs and Excise Department plans a Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System by 2029 [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209].

## Industry benchmarks

- OSL Group Limited (OSL), a listed digital-asset firm, reported in its interim results for the first half of 2026 (Hong Kong and global, reported figures) [I:23e4b81d8271, PDF p.30]. Its payment volume was about HK$61.0 billion, against HK$36.9 billion a year earlier [I:23e4b81d8271, PDF p.30].
- The accounting firm KPMG (China, Hong Kong office) reviewed Hong Kong banks' 2025 accounts in its Hong Kong Banking Report 2026 (reported figures) [I:1dfc7a0205ff, Performance section, page 8]. Surveyed banks spent on average 41.9% of their income on running costs (the cost-to-income ratio) [I:1dfc7a0205ff, Performance section, page 8]. Staff costs rose 6.7% [I:1dfc7a0205ff, Performance section, page 8].
- The same KPMG report (a consultancy view) says many local and regional banks are waiting before building digital-asset capability [I:1dfc7a0205ff, page 42]. It notes that, in the short term, spending on technology, people and compliance can look like cost rather than value [I:1dfc7a0205ff, page 42].

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Does banking digital-asset firms pay for the extra checks it needs?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Income side: deposit balances, payment fees and reserve custody fees from a small number of large clients.
> - Cost side: enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring and reporting for every client, much of it fixed.
> - Concentration: a few clients can bring most of the balances, so losing one client moves the whole result.
> - Example (illustrative): if 2 of 10 platform clients hold most of the deposits, one exit changes the whole result.
> **What it depends on:** the number of licensed platforms and issuers; how much client money and reserves each keeps at banks; fraud and scam trends; monitoring tools.
> **Official signposts:** the SFC platform list [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]; the HKMA's stance on further stablecoin licences [S:193316443831, Follow-up work section, third paragraph]; SFC AML surveillance plans [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)].
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the regulator's view.

- Module [D3 AML/CFT for digital assets at a bank](#m-D3) (AML/CFT: anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing)
- Module [C7 VATP counterparties and the SFC platform regime](#m-C7)
- Module [C4 Stablecoins](#m-C4)

lines.title: Collateral and tokenised financing
lines.md:
In this line a bank lends against digital or tokenised assets, or helps clients use such assets as collateral (security for a loan or trade). (concept)

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Lender; repo counterparty; collateral agent; custodian of pledged assets |
| Client segments | Private banking, corporate, institutional |
| Value chain | Finance, Hold, Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | A bank registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for virtual-asset (VA) dealing may offer VA financing. It is expected to meet the standards in a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) circular [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2] |
| Related modules | [C6](#m-C6), [D1](#m-D1), [C5](#m-C5), [C3](#m-C3), [E2](#m-E2) |
| Related cases | none |
## What the bank does

- Lends to its securities margin clients for VA trading [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2), p.2]. If it relies on VA collateral, the HKMA says it should accept only bitcoin, ether and stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), pp.3-4].
- Applies a haircut (a cut to the collateral's value before lending against it). The HKMA says the haircut on bitcoin and ether should be 60% or more [S:e64b7b0267b2, fn 5, p.4].
- Values VA collateral at prices on the platform that executes the client's orders, as the HKMA generally expects [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6), p.4].
- Keeps pledged virtual assets (VAs) untouched. The bank should not reuse or repledge VA collateral, except to enforce it on default [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(c), p.5].
- Holds or lends against tokenised traditional assets, such as tokenised bonds. (concept) In the banking book, these Group 1a (tokenised traditional) exposures generally follow the capital rules for the underlying asset [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.1].
- Handles tokens used as margin (collateral for trading positions). The SFC's February 2026 high-level framework covers perpetual contracts (futures with no expiry date) on trading platforms. It says their margin should be fiat money, or stablecoins or tokenised deposits regulated by the HKMA [S:49f642bdee28, Margin arrangements section].

## Revenue levers

- A lender earns interest on the loan above its own funding cost. This gap is called the net interest margin. (concept)
- A repo (a sale and agreed buy-back of securities that works like a secured loan) earns a small spread for the cash lender. (concept)
- A collateral agent earns fees for holding, valuing and moving pledged assets between parties. (concept)

## Cost and capital drivers

- Capital: the Banking (Capital) Rules do not recognise VA collateral. So a loan secured only by VAs must be treated as a clean (unsecured) loan [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5].
- Capital: Group 2b cryptoassets take a 1,250% risk weight [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215]. The minimum total capital ratio is 8% [S:5d0c13e09312, para 2.1.2]. So 1,250% × 8% = 100%: at the minimum, the bank holds capital equal to the whole exposure.
- Classification: a bank taking on a new type of cryptoasset must notify the HKMA [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]. It must treat the asset as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees its class [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2].
- Liquidity: the HKMA says fiat loans secured on cryptoassets should be treated like similar deals under the liquidity rules [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 10].
- Liquidity: a category 1 bank must keep a minimum liquidity coverage ratio, a short-term liquidity test [S:69600121310a, para 3.1.2]. It may count a tokenised asset as a high-quality liquid asset only if it is an eligible Group 1a token [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 1].
- Controls: the bank should monitor VA collateral volatility in real time and act promptly [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(b), p.4].

## Official signals

- The 2026 Policy Address states that the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by the end of 2026 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]. These are short-term debt papers the HKMA issues. The stated aim is to help banks use more than HK$1.3 trillion of these bills efficiently, round the clock [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)].
- The Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), the Hong Kong system where bonds are held and settled, held about HK$5 trillion at end-September 2025 [S:9c8855ec55a1, About CMU OmniClear]. Its operator is CMU OmniClear (set up in October 2024). CMU OmniClear offers collateral management among its services [S:9c8855ec55a1, About CMU OmniClear].
- The Project Ensemble Sandbox listed repo and treasury management under its liquidity theme [S:5f8362ecd97f, p.1].
- In April 2026 the HKMA licensed two stablecoin issuers. Its summary of their plans lists collateral management in tokenised asset trading as one use of their coins [S:193316443831, Use cases section].
- Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) aims to pilot tokenised warehouse-receipt financing with chosen banks in 2027 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 46(iv)].
- In June 2026 the HKMA clarified a Group 1 condition for tokenised traditional assets on public blockchains. The condition can now also be met where a financial market regulator supervises the tokenisation business [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1].

## Industry benchmarks

- A 2025 report by the Global Financial Markets Association (GFMA) and other trade bodies (global, modelled) cites a study by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) and Ripple [I:7f93581e44fe, PDF p.10]. That modelled estimate says a bank running about US$100 billion of daily repo could save US$150–300 million a year [I:7f93581e44fe, PDF p.10].
- The GFMA's 2025 case studies (global, operator-reported) put one ledger-based repo platform at about US$1.5 trillion a month in late 2024 [I:04d8f959d7a3, p.14].
- The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) published a report in 2025 (global, survey). In its 2024 survey of members, 91% of respondents reported nil or very limited commercial tokenisation use in their markets [I:5f69773bc91f, p.13, section 3.B.1].

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Where does tokenised collateral create value for a bank: in new lending, or in cheaper use of assets it already holds?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Lending view: VA-backed loans carry no capital relief for the collateral [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]. The income then has to cover the full capital charge on an unsecured loan.
> - Balance-sheet view: tokenised high-quality assets could move faster between the bank's own teams and its counterparties. In this view, value would come from holding less spare collateral, not from new fees.
> - Service view: holding and valuing collateral for others earns fees without the bank lending its own money.
> **What it depends on:** how the tokenised bill tests are designed; whether counterparties accept tokens; legal certainty on pledges; capital treatment.
> **Official signposts:** tokenised Exchange Fund Bill tests [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]; the HKEX warehouse-receipt pilot [S:ef3648ff1610, para 46(iv)]; the April 2026 capital-rule proposal on cryptoassets and cash items [S:1e9b351e81e7, Item 45].
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the regulator's view.

- Module [C6 Financing, shared order books and client withdrawals](#m-C6)
- Module [D1 Capital and prudential treatment of cryptoassets](#m-D1)
- Module [C5 Tokenisation: tokenised products, deposits and bonds](#m-C5)

lines.title: Cross-border payments, FX and mBridge
lines.md:
A bank can do foreign exchange (FX) and send money abroad through new systems, such as shared digital-currency platforms, tokenised deposits and licensed stablecoins. (concept)

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Payment bank; FX provider; wallet top-up bank; settlement bank |
| Client segments | Retail, corporate, institutional, fintechs |
| Value chain | Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | A banking licence; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) also expects banks to discuss new digital-asset activities with it before launch [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (2)] |
| Related modules | [E2](#m-E2), [C4](#m-C4), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3) |
| Related cases | [Case 2: Tokenised deposits for corporate treasury](#case-2-tokenised-deposits-treasury) |
## What the bank does

- Project mBridge studies how central bank digital currency (CBDC) can solve problems in cross-border payments. [S:db56d97e2206, para 2]
- mBridge reached its minimum viable product (MVP) stage in June 2024. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] The Government says it now forms part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] On mBridge, the payer's bank and the payee's bank settle with each other directly. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- In the 2022 pilot, foreign banks could hold and use another place's CBDC. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, p.32] Only that place's own banks could get it issued, or swap it back for central bank reserves. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, p.32]
- The 2022 pilot report says each bank on mBridge stays bound by its own anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorist financing (CFT) and sanctions laws. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35] The bank checks each payment off the platform and attaches a pass or fail result. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]
- Eighteen local banks let users top up e-CNY (the digital renminbi) wallets through the Faster Payment System (FPS). [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]
- HKMA custody guidance allows transfers of client digital assets to third parties to support payment services, with effective risk controls in place. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m)]

## Revenue levers

- Hong Kong banks on mBridge set their own cross-border payment fees. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] They base the fees on their operating costs and commercial needs. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- An FX spread is the gap between the rate a bank gets in the market and the rate it gives the client. (concept)
- Money waiting to be paid out sits with the bank as a balance it can earn on. (concept)
- The HKMA lists cross-border payments for companies and individuals among the key use cases of both licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:193316443831, Use cases and strategic priorities section] A bank serving stablecoin users can charge for converting, holding and paying out coins. (concept)
- The HKMA now puts wholesale uses of the e-HKD (a digital Hong Kong dollar) first. Wholesale uses are those between banks and other large institutions. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] Those uses include cross-border payments such as settling international trade. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]

## Cost and capital drivers

- A bank should complete customer due diligence (CDD) before a one-off (occasional) wire or virtual-asset transfer of HK$8,000 or more. [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1(b)(ii)-(iii)] It should also watch for linked smaller transfers that reach that level together. [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.4]
- The "travel rule" means sending payer and payee details along with a transfer. (concept) The HKMA has an AML guideline for licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, para 6.5] Under it, a sending issuer must record payer and payee details before a stablecoin transfer of HK$8,000 or more. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, para 6.5]
- The HKMA's liquidity guidance keeps CBDC out of its cryptoasset annex. [S:69600121310a, para 5.9.3] CBDC may generally be treated like the issuing place's notes and coins, subject to each CBDC's features and legal status. [S:69600121310a, para 5.9.3]
- The mBridge team is helping banks link their systems to the platform's application programming interface (API). [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] Each link is a build and running cost for the bank. (concept)
- In correspondent banking, a bank parks cash in advance in accounts at banks abroad. Direct settlement can cut the cash parked this way. (concept)

## Official signals

- In the 2022 mBridge pilot, 20 banks from four places made over 160 payment and FX deals worth over US$22 million. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4]
- By end-January 2026, about 80,000 e-CNY wallets had been set up with Hong Kong mobile numbers. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)] About 5,200 local shops accepted e-CNY. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]
- In June 2025 the HKMA and the People's Bank of China (PBoC) launched Payment Connect. [S:efc2e3e27f62, p.136, Faster Payment System section] It links the FPS with a Mainland online banking payment system for real-time remittances. [S:efc2e3e27f62, p.136, Faster Payment System section]
- The Government's November 2025 digital green bond offered settlement in tokenised central bank money (e-CNY and e-HKD). [S:ac6cd085a325, Integration of digital money item] This option sat alongside traditional settlement. [S:ac6cd085a325, Integration of digital money item] The Government said it was the world's first digital bond offering to do so. [S:ac6cd085a325, Integration of digital money item]
- Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) and the HKMA are working together on an e-HKD payment tool for after-hours derivatives trading. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] Real-value deals are targeted for 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)]
- The HKMA is testing CBDC networks, tokenised deposits and links between fast payment systems. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (2)] Both licensed stablecoin issuers take part. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (2)]

## Industry benchmarks

- The Financial Stability Board (FSB) published a global progress report in 2025, using reported data. It put the global average cost of sending a US$200 remittance at 6.5%. [I:0c779bbbb00d, p.27, section 3.3]
- The same FSB report (reported, Asia-Pacific scope) said only 25.6% of wholesale cross-border payments into the region arrived within one hour. [I:0c779bbbb00d, p.27, section 3.4.1]
- The same report said person-to-person payments sent from East Asia and the Pacific cost 3% on average. [I:0c779bbbb00d, p.28, section 3.4.1] It gives no Hong Kong-only figure.

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** If new systems make each cross-border payment faster and cheaper, where does a bank still earn?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Split income into three parts: the fee per payment, the FX spread, and balances held along the way.
> - Faster systems can cut the fee per payment but can raise the number of payments.
> - A bank can join as a direct participant, or serve smaller banks and fintechs that connect through it.
> - Compliance cost per payment stays, because each bank runs its own checks.
> **What it depends on:** which currency routes clients use; how many central banks and banks connect; stablecoin use; the cost of AML checks per payment.
> **Official signposts:**
> - Fees on mBridge are set by each bank. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
> - The e-HKD tool for after-hours derivatives. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)]
> - The HKMA's testing of new payment options with the stablecoin licensees. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (2)]
> **What this is not:** not a forecast, not advice and not the regulator's view.

lines.title: Virtual-asset custody
lines.md:
In this line a bank safekeeps clients' digital assets, such as virtual assets (VAs) and tokenised securities (securities recorded as digital tokens) [S:ed61d7c335e7, fn 1, p.1]. It also guards the private keys (the secret codes that control the assets) [S:ed61d7c335e7, fn 1, p.1].

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Custodian; custodian that funds and other firms appoint to hold assets for them |
| Client segments | Retail, private banking, institutional, fintechs |
| Value chain | Hold, Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) expects the bank to discuss plans with it first and show it meets the HKMA custody standards [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Related modules | [C3](#m-C3), [C2](#m-C2), [C1](#m-C1), [D1](#m-D1), [D4](#m-D4) |
| Related cases | [Case 1: Virtual-asset custody for private banking](#case-1-va-custody-private-banking) |
## What the bank does

- Keeps client assets and wallet addresses separate from its own, as the HKMA expects, so they stay out of reach of the bank's creditors [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 6 and fn 6].
- Keeps 98% of client VAs in cold storage (keys held offline), as the HKMA expects [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8].
- Creates, stores and backs up private keys for client VAs in Hong Kong, a control the HKMA generally requires [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b)].
- Holds assets for funds. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) lets the trustee of a VA fund it authorises hand VA custody to a bank that meets HKMA standards [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 20].
- Acts as custodian for other banks, SFC-licensed firms and licensed platforms that keep their clients' assets in an account with the bank [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 9].
- Sends client assets to other parties to make payments or settle client trades, if effective controls are in place [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m)].

## Revenue levers

- A custody fee is usually a yearly percentage of the value held, sometimes with a monthly minimum. (concept)
- Fund custody fees may be bundled with administration fees. The sub-custodian (a second custodian holding the assets for the main one) is then paid from that bundle. (concept)
- Staking (locking client VAs so they help run a blockchain, for a reward) is a further lever. The HKMA has issued staking guidance that is separate from its custody guidance [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26].
- Holding a client's assets also opens the way to other income from the same client, such as dealing, fund servicing and lending. (concept)

## Cost and capital drivers

- Liability: the HKMA expects the bank to be liable for losses from incidents it causes [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]. The bank should hold adequate financial resources, which may include insurance [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- Operations: security monitoring should run around the clock [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23]. Holdings should be checked client by client against records on the blockchain and in the bank's own books [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21].
- Outsourcing: as a general principle, a bank may delegate VA custody only to three kinds of firm [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]. They are another bank or a local bank's subsidiary, an SFC-licensed platform, or an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer for its own coins with HKMA consent [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]. Final responsibility stays with the bank [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 19].
- New licence: banks that safekeep client VA keys would need a licence or registration under the planned regime [S:f41a543388bc, para 35(b)]. The Government and the SFC do not plan to treat existing VA custodians as licensed while they apply [S:f41a543388bc, para 48]. The regime takes full effect on its start date [S:f41a543388bc, para 48].
- Capital: the planned minimum of HK$10 million paid-up capital (money put in by shareholders) does not apply to banks [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42]. The reason is that HKMA capital rules already cover them [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42].
- Technology: the SFC says its August 2025 custody standards for trading platforms will be core expectations for future custodians [S:562c0f8addce, p.2].

## Official signals

- The SFC listed 13 licensed VA trading platforms at its 29 May 2026 update [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; Last update line].
- Hong Kong had 11 VA spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs) at end-2025, with a total market value of over HK$5.4 billion [S:c28638fc5ccc, para 4].
- The SFC and the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau aim to put a custodian bill to the Legislative Council in 2026 [S:f41a543388bc, para 65].
- Banks the HKMA has already assessed, and that already provide VA custody, are to get faster approval [S:f41a543388bc, para 51].
- Under the planned dealing regime, the SFC will require VA dealers to use SFC-regulated custodians [S:6186c01c6649, para 26].
- The SFC plans to begin running a system to watch digital-asset custody in the second half of 2026 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)].

## Industry benchmarks

- China Asset Management (Hong Kong) gives a fee in its April 2026 key facts statement, a short summary of a fund (Hong Kong scope) [I:ee50e4efff6f, PDF p.11]. Its ether fund pays up to 1% a year for custody and administration [I:ee50e4efff6f, PDF p.11]. That fee also pays the sub-custodian [I:ee50e4efff6f, PDF p.11].
- Bosera Asset Management (International) describes how its sub-custodian covers losses, in a March 2026 Hong Kong fund prospectus [I:d81073907a14, PDF p.118]. Compensation or insurance covers 50% of client VAs in cold storage [I:d81073907a14, PDF p.118]. The cover is 100% for VAs in hot storage (keys online) and other storage [I:d81073907a14, PDF p.118].
- OSL Group Limited (OSL) reported custody income in its 2025 annual report (Hong Kong and global scope) [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.126, Note 5]. It was about HK$16.1 million in 2025, up from about HK$9.6 million in 2024 [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.126, Note 5].

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Is VA custody a fee business on its own, or mainly the base that lets other lines run?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Standalone view: income equals assets held times the fee rate. Costs for keys, monitoring, audit and insurance start before any assets arrive, and are largely fixed.
> - Enabler view: count the dealing, fund, staking and settlement income that needs a custodian in place.
> - Build or delegate: the bank can run its own key systems, or hand custody to a licensed platform. If it hands custody over, responsibility still stays with the bank [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 19].
> **What it depends on:** client asset levels; fee pressure from fund issuers; insurance cost; the final custodian rules and their start date.
> **Official signposts:** the custodian bill target [S:f41a543388bc, para 65]; SFC work on more flexible custody technology and on how much is kept offline [S:f41a543388bc, para 38]; custodian use under the dealing regime [S:6186c01c6649, para 26].
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the regulator's view.

lines.title: Digital bonds: arranging and custody
lines.md:
In this line a bank arranges, sells, holds or invests in bonds recorded on distributed ledger technology (DLT), a shared digital record (concept).

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Arranger; distributor; custodian for investors; investor |
| Client segments | Corporate, institutional, private banking |
| Value chain | Issue, Distribute, Hold, Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | Existing securities licences and offering rules apply to digital bonds [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11]. A bank should notify the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) in advance [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 7] |
| Related modules | [C5](#m-C5), [B2](#m-B2), [E2](#m-E2) |
| Related cases | [Case 5: The board's strategic plan](#case-5-board-strategic-plan) |
## What the bank does

- Arranges issues. For the HKMA's Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS), at least half the lead arrangers need to be recognised arrangers [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3]. These are generally arrangers with substantial Hong Kong bond operations [S:5a0563de8142, fn 4, p.3].
- Sells to investors. The Government's first tokenised green bond was sold by a group of four banks [S:a0841967c871, para 2]. Two of them also acted as custodians for investors [S:a0841967c871, para 2].
- Holds bonds for clients. Project Evergreen was the Government's 2023 tokenised bond. In it, only custodians that were members of the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), the HKMA's bond settlement system, could open token accounts [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16]. Other investors held through those custodians [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16].
- Checks the product. The SFC reminds intermediaries to do due diligence on the issuer and on the vendors that run the token set-up [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 17].
- Judges complexity. The SFC expects an intermediary to judge whether a tokenised bond is complex by looking at the plain bond underneath [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 24].
- Sells beyond professional investors. The SFC sees no need for a blanket professional-investor-only limit on tokenised securities [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 26]. Public offering rules still apply [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 27].

## Revenue levers

- Arranging fees are usually a small share of the amount raised, paid by the issuer (concept).
- Custody fees are usually a small yearly share of the bonds held for the client (concept).
- The DBGS pays back half of an issuer's eligible costs, up to HK$2.5 million per issue [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2]. Eligible costs include fees to Hong Kong-based arrangers and to ledger platform providers [S:5a0563de8142, s.4, p.5].

## Cost and capital drivers

- Settlement finality: trades settled through the CMU are final by law, so a participant's insolvency cannot reverse them [S:a0b44be27c40, para 36, p.14]. Another ledger platform gets this only if the HKMA designates it [S:a0b44be27c40, para 37, p.15]. Otherwise the parties rely on their contracts [S:a0b44be27c40, para 38, p.15].
- Grant conditions: among other things, the full grant needs an issue of at least HK$1 billion and five or more unrelated investors [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]. It also needs a listing on the Hong Kong stock exchange or an SFC-licensed virtual asset trading platform [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4].
- Technology: the bank builds its own ledger links or pays a platform provider (concept).
- Risk controls: the SFC expects intermediaries to manage ownership and technology risks on top of normal bond rules [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 8].

## Official signals

- The 2026 Policy Address says digital bonds issued in Hong Kong took nearly 50% of the global market over 2025 and the first half of 2026 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35].
- The Government's November 2025 digital green bond raised about HK$10 billion, with over HK$130 billion of orders [S:ac6cd085a325, para 1; Expanding scale section]. The Government said it was the first digital bond in the world to offer settlement in tokenised central bank money (digital cash issued by a central bank) [S:ac6cd085a325, Integration of digital money section].
- In June 2026 the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) priced about HK$12 billion of digital bonds [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]. Settlement fell from five business days to three [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 5].
- In the 2026-27 Budget, the Financial Secretary said the Government will keep issuing tokenised bonds regularly [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97].
- CMU OmniClear (the HKMA's bond-settlement company) is to set up a digital asset platform for bond issuance and settlement in 2026 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)].
- The Companies Registry confirmed that a register of debenture holders (bond investors) kept on a ledger can meet company-law record rules [S:279f10054c6e, Issuing clarifications section].

## Industry benchmarks

- The Bank for International Settlements (BIS), 2025 staff bulletin (global, reported): about US$8 billion of tokenised bonds had been issued by July 2025 [I:44ec1038876d, PDF p.3]. The authors call their evidence suggestive; their matched sample has 39 bonds [I:44ec1038876d, PDF p.3].
- The same BIS bulletin found average bid-ask spreads of about 19 basis points for tokenised bonds, against 30 for matched plain bonds [I:44ec1038876d, PDF p.5]. A bid-ask spread is the gap between buying and selling prices; a basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point.
- The Global Financial Markets Association (GFMA) 2025 report (global) relays a modelled estimate by Ripple and Boston Consulting Group [I:7f93581e44fe, PDF p.10]. That estimate says tokenising an investment-grade bond can cut operating costs by 40–60% against a traditional issue [I:7f93581e44fe, PDF p.10].

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Is a digital bond desk a new source of fees, or the same arranging and custody fees earned through new technology?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Same-fee view: the issuer pays for arranging, selling and custody as with a plain bond. The ledger changes how the bond is recorded and settled, not the price.
> - Share view: the grant's Hong Kong test counts recognised arrangers [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3]. Do arranging jobs then go mainly to banks already on that list that are also CMU custodians?
> - Cost view: faster settlement and fewer manual steps can lower the bank's own running cost per issue.
> - Example (illustrative): if a desk arranges 4 issues a year at an unchanged fee rate, any gain comes from less staff time per deal.
> **What it depends on:** the number of issuers beyond the public sector; how many issuers use the grant; investor demand to trade after issue; platform and custody fees.
> **Official signposts:** regular Government issuance [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97]; the CMU OmniClear platform [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]; the second-phase legal review [S:279f10054c6e, Next phase section].
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the regulator's view.

## Read next

lines.md:
A bank can run, or sell access to, the technology behind digital assets: shared ledgers, token-issuing tools, custody systems and settlement links. (concept)

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Platform operator; technology provider; settlement bank; custodian for other firms |
| Client segments | Corporate, institutional, fintechs |
| Value chain | Issue, Hold, Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) expectations on distributed ledger technology (DLT) and custody. The HKMA also expects banks to discuss new digital-asset activities with it before launch [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 1-4 and 8; S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3] |
| Related modules | [B3](#m-B3), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D4](#m-D4), [E2](#m-E2) |
| Related cases | [Case 4: The night the hot wallet emptied](#case-4-vatp-incident) |
## What the bank does

- A bank can test DLT projects with a dedicated HKMA team in the Supervisory Incubator. [S:fae36c380174, p.1] The HKMA may give some supervisory flexibility, decided case by case. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and fn 2]
- In the Ensemble Sandbox, banks connected their own tokenised deposit platforms to an HKMA settlement set-up. [S:460620ab7f2b, para 2] A tokenised deposit is a bank deposit recorded as a token on a shared ledger. (concept)
- As a general principle, a bank may hand virtual-asset (VA) custody to only three kinds of firm. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14] The first is another bank, or a subsidiary of a locally incorporated bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14] The second is a VA trading platform holding a Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licence. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14] The third is an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer, for its own coins and with HKMA consent. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- Issuing on a DLT platform run by the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) is one route into the Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS). [S:5a0563de8142, s.2 and fn 6, p.3]
- The HKMA formed the Ensemble Architecture Community in May 2024 to write industry standards. [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-2] The standards aim to link wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC), tokenised money and tokenised assets. [S:0169bc8fbb4d, para 2]

## Revenue levers

- Software as a service (SaaS) means a client rents a platform instead of building its own, often for a base fee plus a usage fee. (concept)
- Other banks can outsource VA custody to a bank, which makes custody a service one bank can sell to another. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- DBGS grants can repay issuers' fees to DLT platform providers that are not the issuer's associates (firms linked to the issuer). [S:5a0563de8142, s.4(a), p.5] The full grant, up to HK$2.5 million per issue, needs such an outside platform, among other conditions. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3(a), p.4]
- A settlement bank can charge for moving tokenised money between parties, or keep the balances that clients hold with it. (concept)

## Cost and capital drivers

- The HKMA's DLT note puts responsibility on the board and senior management. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 1-4 and 8] It covers network choice, smart contracts, settlement finality and key security. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 1-4 and 8]
- A hardware security module (HSM) is a tamper-resistant device that stores keys. (concept) Banks should check HSM vendors before onboarding and review them regularly. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)] A bank's custody monitoring should cover vendors, blockchain protocols, encryption methods and shared code libraries. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 24]
- For tokenised products, banks should check issuers' technology, including smart-contract audits, key management and plans for ledger failure. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- For SFC-authorised tokenised products, the product provider stays responsible for the token set-up even if it outsources it. [S:58ea8520974d, para 10] On SFC request, it should get an outside audit of the set-up and its smart contracts. [S:58ea8520974d, para 15]
- The HKMA has launched a Quantum Preparedness Index to guide the industry on upgrading encryption. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(ii)]
- The HKMA plans a Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline for technology firms that serve banks with DLT and artificial intelligence tools. [S:b0607b779270, paras 3-6]

## Official signals

- EnsembleTX (the live pilot of the HKMA's Project Ensemble) is to run throughout 2026. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3] It is to move step by step to round-the-clock settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
- EnsembleTX named 13 other industry pioneers besides its banks, including asset managers, technology firms and Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX). [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex B, p.2]
- In November 2025 the HKMA announced that HKEX would take a 20% stake in the holding company of CMU OmniClear (the CMU's operator). [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] The Exchange Fund would hold 80%. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] Assets held in the CMU were about HK$5 trillion at end-September 2025. [S:9c8855ec55a1, About CMU OmniClear section]
- CMU OmniClear is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] It is to be widened to other digital assets and linked to other platforms in the region. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]
- HKEX is building a blockchain-based tokenisation platform for many asset types, which already holds carbon credits. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 46(v)]
- In an HKMA stock-take run in January 2025 and published in July 2025, 45% of respondents had adopted DLT, up from 30% in 2022. [S:738405ae090d, p.11]

## Industry benchmarks

- OSL Group Limited (OSL) is a Hong Kong-listed platform group. It reported 2025 SaaS and related income of HK$133.1 million, against HK$91.6 million in 2024. [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.126, Note 5] These are group figures, not Hong Kong only.
- OSL's 2025 annual report says its SaaS fees are typically based on a base fee plus the trading volume of the client's platform. [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.91, Note 2.2.3]
- KPMG (a professional services firm) published a 2026 Hong Kong banking report through KPMG China. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, p.42] Its commentary says spending on technology, talent and cybersecurity can look like cost rather than value in the short term. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, p.42] KPMG sells advisory services to banks.

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** When does running shared digital-asset infrastructure pay back for a bank, compared with renting it?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Building a platform has a high fixed cost and a low cost per extra client. So the number of clients decides whether it pays back.
> - Public platforms, such as the planned CMU OmniClear platform, can compete with a bank platform or connect to it.
> - Clients that rent the platform stay answerable to their own regulators. How much due diligence and audit work then comes with each sale?
> - Renting avoids the build cost but leaves the bank reliant on a vendor that then needs close monitoring.
> **What it depends on:** the number of client firms; standards that let platforms connect; vendor and audit costs; how liability for failures is shared.
> **Official signposts:**
> - The CMU OmniClear digital asset platform. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]
> - Round-the-clock settlement in EnsembleTX. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
> - Standards from the Ensemble Architecture Community that let platforms connect (interoperability). [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (3)]
> **What this is not:** not a forecast, not advice and not the regulator's view.

lines.title: Stablecoin roles for banks
lines.md:
A bank can issue a stablecoin, hold the issuer's reserves, sell or trade the coin, or lend against it (concept).

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Issuer; reserve bank and custodian; distributor and dealer; lender that takes coins as collateral |
| Client segments | Retail, private banking, corporate, institutional, fintechs |
| Value chain | Issue, Distribute, Trade, Hold, Settle and pay, Finance |
| Regulatory gate | Issuing needs a stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.7.1] Banks may offer licensed coins to investors as 'permitted offerors' (firms the law allows to offer stablecoins). [S:7b6c8dc63140, Reply (1)] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, opening para] |
| Related modules | [C4](#m-C4), [C1](#m-C1), [C6](#m-C6), [D1](#m-D1), [D3](#m-D3) |
| Related cases | [Case 3: The reserve bank that also sells the coin](#case-3-stablecoin-reserve-distributor) |
## What the bank does

A stablecoin is a token meant to keep a steady value against a currency (concept).

- **Issue.** A bank may apply for an issuer licence. A bank incorporated overseas does not need a Hong Kong subsidiary. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3]
- **Hold reserves.** The HKMA says issuers should appoint qualified custodians (firms that safekeep assets) for reserves. A licensed bank is one eligible custodian. [S:240be6833157, para 2.5.4]
- **Take reserve deposits.** Reserves may include bank deposits with terms of up to three months. [S:240be6833157, para 2.3.1] In June 2026 the Government said that, under HKMA rules, issuers place reserve assets with banks in Hong Kong. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (1)]
- **Sell.** Banks are one of five types of permitted offeror. They may offer licensed coins to retail and professional investors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, Reply (1)]
- **Deal.** A bank registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) is a registered institution (RI). An RI may deal in licensed coins through the issuer or a licensed virtual asset trading platform (VATP). [S:a0bd48559762, paras (1), (3)(c), pp.3-5]
- **Lend.** An RI may choose to accept crypto as collateral for loans. If so, the HKMA says eligible collateral should be only bitcoin, ether and licensed coins. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), pp.3-4] The RI should apply a prudent haircut (a discount on the collateral's value). [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), pp.3-4]

## Revenue levers

- **Reserve deposits.** A bank holding reserve deposits earns the gap between what it earns on the money and what it pays for it (concept).
- **Issuer income.** An issuer that pays holders nothing keeps the return on its reserves, less its costs (concept). The Stablecoins Ordinance bars issuers from paying interest to holders. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1]
- **Custody and sales fees.** A custodian charges fees on the value it holds, and a seller earns a commission or a price spread (concept).
- **Payments.** A bank can charge fees for moving money into and out of coins (concept). Both licensed issuers plan cross-border payments, local payments and settling tokenised asset trades. [S:193316443831, Use cases and strategic priorities section]

## Cost and capital drivers

- **Issuer capital.** A licensed issuer must keep paid-up capital of at least HK$25 million, or other approved resources of the same amount. [S:240be6833157, para 5.1.1] A bank licensee is exempt and follows the Banking Ordinance instead. [S:240be6833157, para 5.1.3]
- **Redemption.** Issuers must let holders redeem at par (face value). [S:240be6833157, para 3.3.1] Valid requests should be processed within one business day unless the HKMA approves otherwise. [S:240be6833157, para 3.3.3]
- **Liquidity.** The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) tests whether a bank has enough liquid assets for a short stress period. A category 1 bank (one that must meet the LCR) that issues a coin redeemable in that period must generally assume that the whole amount flows out. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] A category 1 bank holding such a coin generally counts no cash inflow from it. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
- **Capital.** HKMA guidance puts stablecoins with effective stabilisation (a working way to keep their value steady) in Group 1b, one of the capital groups for cryptoassets. Group 1 assets generally need the same capital as the traditional assets they are linked to. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.3.2]
- **Anti-money laundering (AML).** An issuer should check customers before a one-off (occasional) transaction of HK$8,000 or more. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, para 4.4] For transfers at or above that amount, the sending firm must obtain and record fuller sender and recipient data. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.5-6.6]

## Official signals

- The HKMA received 36 first-batch applications by 30 September 2025. It licensed two issuers on 10 April 2026. [S:193316443831, Assessment of licence applications, paras 1-2]
- The register lists two licensees from 10 April 2026: Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02). [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- Both issuers plan Hong Kong dollar coins first. [S:193316443831, Use cases and strategic priorities section]
- On 28 April 2026 both licensees confirmed they had not yet issued regulated stablecoins. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]
- In April 2026 the HKMA expected launch between mid-2026 and the second half of 2026, based on the issuers' plans. [S:193316443831, Follow-up work, para 1]
- On 16 September 2026 a Government spokesman said the first regulated stablecoin in Hong Kong had launched in August 2026. [S:8be6d15c6641, para 10] The official sources reviewed do not name the issuer.
- The Government said any further licences will stay very limited in number. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]

## Industry benchmarks

- The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) gave a global, reported market figure in its 2026 Annual Economic Report. It put stablecoin value at about US$320 billion at end-May 2026. [I:efa37f6d77e9, p. 88]
- A 2025 BIS Bulletin, also global in scope, reported that two issuers held about 90% of stablecoin value in mid-2025. [I:2f192e0e1c86, p. 2, Graph 1.B]
- Circle Internet Group, a US-listed issuer, reported in its own results filing US$733 million of reserve income for the fourth quarter of 2025. It reported US$461 million of distribution, transaction and other costs for the same quarter. [I:c835a8109c3f, Fourth Quarter 2025 Financial Highlights]
- These are global reported figures, not Hong Kong figures.

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Which stablecoin role could suit a bank that does not issue a coin?
> **How to think about it:** List each role by what it earns and what it uses up. Reserve banking earns a deposit margin, but the money can leave fast when holders redeem. Selling and dealing earn fees per trade. They need conduct controls (fair treatment of clients) and AML controls. Lending earns interest and uses capital.
> **What it depends on:** How widely licensed coins circulate after the first launch. How reserve deposit terms fit liquidity limits. Client demand for payment uses. The cost of monitoring transfers.
> **Official signposts:** News of further launches, which the HKMA tied to the issuers' plans. [S:193316443831, Follow-up work, para 1] Any further licences. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)] SFC steps to promote trading of licensed coins on licensed platforms and their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the HKMA's or SFC's view.

- Module [C1 Selling, dealing and advising on virtual assets](#m-C1)
- Module [C6 Financing, shared order books and client withdrawals](#m-C6)

lines.title: Staking services
lines.md:
A bank that holds virtual assets (VAs) for clients may lock them up to help confirm transactions on a blockchain, and pass the rewards to those clients. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Custodian that stakes client VAs; staking provider to brokers and funds |
| Client segments | Retail, private banking, institutional |
| Value chain | Hold |
| Regulatory gate | Meet the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) staking standards and discuss plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, Implementation, p.3] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] |
| Related modules | [C3](#m-C3), [C1](#m-C1), [C2](#m-C2), [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3) |
| Related cases | [Case 6: Stopping a product](#case-6-stopping-a-product) |
## What the bank does

- Banks, and subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks, may offer staking from their custody services under HKMA standards dated 7 April 2025. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1]
- Staking means locking tokens so a validator can take part in a proof-of-stake network and earn rewards. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] A validator runs the computers that confirm new blocks, and puts up tokens as a stake to earn that role. (concept)
- The HKMA says a bank must do all reasonable due diligence on a blockchain before it offers staking on it. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (C), p.2] The bank must also make sure its controls and systems can support staking on that chain. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (C), p.2]
- A bank may outsource staking work to a third party. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (C), p.3] It should check that provider first and then keep monitoring it. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (C), p.3]
- Other firms can use a bank as their staking provider. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.2] The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) sets terms for licensed corporations, such as brokers, and for registered institutions, which are banks registered with it. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.2] Under those terms, they should stake client assets only through an SFC-licensed platform or a bank. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.2]
- The SFC may let the virtual-asset funds it authorises stake through licensed platforms or banks. [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28, 31] Such funds need prior consultation with, and approval from, the SFC. [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28, 31]

## Revenue levers

- A staking provider can keep a share of the network rewards and pass the rest to the client. It can also charge a fee on staked assets instead. (concept)
- The HKMA expects a bank to disclose its staking fees and charges. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (B), p.2] It should also disclose lock-up and unstaking periods. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (B), p.2]
- Licensed corporations and registered institutions should tell clients the fees agreed with their staking provider and how those fees are worked out. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.7(d)]
- An SFC-authorised fund that stakes should report the revenue and the direct and indirect costs of its staking. [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 28(f)]
- Staking gives clients a return on assets that would otherwise sit idle in custody. That can help a bank keep custody balances. (concept)

## Cost and capital drivers

- The HKMA expects a bank to control everything needed to take client assets out of staking. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (A) and fn 2, p.2] Examples are the withdrawal keys and exit messages signed in advance. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (A) and fn 2, p.2]
- A bank should explain the extra risks of staking. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (B), p.2] The circular lists slashing risk, lock-up risk, software bugs and hacking among them. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (B), p.2] Slashing is a network penalty that takes away part of a validator's staked tokens. (concept)
- The bank should also say how such losses would be dealt with. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (B), p.2] Who bears a slashing loss depends on the contracts between client, bank and validator. (concept)
- Licensed corporations and registered institutions should get a signed risk acknowledgement from most clients. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.8] Institutional and qualified corporate professional investors are the exception. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.8]
- Checking an outside staking provider covers its track record, technology, risk measures and security controls. [S:4641e6c404d2, section (C), p.3]
- A firm that stops staking should take due account of clients' best interests. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.6] It should explain their options, such as unstaking. [S:31b4f67e0233, para 8.6]

## Official signals

- In April 2025 the SFC set out staking guidance for platforms and funds under the Products pillar of its roadmap. [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]
- That SFC roadmap, called ASPIRe, listed staking as something to consider under clear custody and operating rules. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar P, Initiative 8]
- In September 2025 the SFC and HKMA said they are now prepared to let intermediaries offer staking. [S:b79266f3da51, para 4]
- Intermediaries should tell the regulators before they offer staking for the first time. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10(c)]
- The HKMA's May 2026 custody guidance asks banks to take account of the SFC's staking terms for platforms. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26]
- In April 2025 the SFC said the virtual-asset funds it authorises are required to stake only through licensed platforms and banks. It added that a cap applies, to manage liquidity risk. [S:36753b22e10a, para 4]

## Industry benchmarks

- HashKey Holdings (HashKey), a Hong Kong-listed platform group, reported group-wide figures in its 2025 annual results. It gave its own measure, a staking "monetization rate", of 0.2%, down from 0.3% in 2024. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.4] The results do not give its formula. The same report gave average staked assets of about HK$22.4 billion. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.4]
- HashKey's 2026 interim results, also a company filing, reported average staked assets of HK$14.8 billion in the first half. [I:9ca15dca711d, PDF p.11] The same report gave HK$20.2 billion a year earlier. [I:9ca15dca711d, PDF p.11]
- Coinbase Global's 2025 annual report, global in scope, reported US$677.4 million of blockchain rewards revenue for 2025. [I:6fc50821b9ab, PDF p.94] The same report showed US$427.5 million of blockchain rewards fees as a cost. [I:6fc50821b9ab, PDF p.95]
- China Asset Management (Hong Kong) published a key facts statement for its Hong Kong-listed ether exchange-traded fund (ETF) in April 2026. It said the fund intends to stake up to 30% of its ether. [I:ee50e4efff6f, PDF p.2]

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Is staking a profit line in its own right, or a feature that keeps custody clients?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Staking income is roughly staked assets times the network reward rate times the bank's share. (concept)
> - Costs include validator fees, key-control systems, disclosure work and handling losses.
> - A small share of rewards on a large pool of custody assets can earn more than a large share on a small pool.
> **What it depends on:** network reward rates; token prices; client interest; the share the bank keeps; who bears slashing losses; vendor costs.
> **Official signposts:**
> - The SFC staking terms that banks take account of. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26]
> - Notice to regulators before a firm first offers staking. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10(c)]
> - Faster licensing for banks already assessed for custody. [S:f41a543388bc, para 51]
> **What this is not:** not a forecast, not advice and not the regulator's view.

- Module [C1 Selling, dealing and advising on virtual assets](#m-C1)

lines.title: Tokenised deposits and payments
lines.md:
A bank can record customer deposits as tokens on a shared digital ledger and use them to pay and settle around the clock. (concept)

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Bank role | Issuer; settlement bank; payment provider |
| Client segments | Corporate, institutional, fintechs |
| Value chain | Issue, Settle and pay |
| Regulatory gate | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) standards for tokenised products, and talks with the HKMA before launch [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 fn 1; Implementation, p.6] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |
| Related modules | [C5](#m-C5), [E2](#m-E2), [D1](#m-D1), [B2](#m-B2) |
| Related cases | [Case 2: Tokenised deposits for corporate treasury](#case-2-tokenised-deposits-treasury) |
## What the bank does

- The HKMA's liquidity guidance covers tokens a bank issues that are a legally binding claim on that bank. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4] To fall in this group, the tokens must be redeemable in cash at face value. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
- The HKMA expects a bank to apply its tokenised-products standards when customers place tokenised deposits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 fn 1]
- A "Tokenised Deposit Bank" in the HKMA pilot offers tokenised deposits to Hong Kong customers. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A, p.1] It also settles tokenised-deposit deals with other banks using real money. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A, p.1]
- That pilot, EnsembleTX (the live phase of the HKMA's Project Ensemble), started on 13 November 2025. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1]
- Its first uses are paying for tokenised money market fund (MMF) trades and managing liquidity and treasury needs in real time. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 2]
- Before a full launch, a bank can test its controls in the HKMA's Supervisory Incubator for distributed ledger technology (DLT). [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] Tokenised deposits were a core focus from its launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

## Revenue levers

- Deposits fund a bank's lending and investing. The gap between what the bank earns on that money and what it pays depositors is its net interest margin. (concept)
- Corporate clients can pay fees for services built on tokens, such as automatic sweeps (moving cash between accounts by set rules) and payments that run at set times. (concept)
- Tokenised deposits can pay for tokenised fund trades, which is an initial EnsembleTX focus. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 2]
- The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has set out a pilot for 24/7 (round-the-clock) secondary trading of tokenised products. [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4] The SFC said trading could use regulated stablecoins and tokenised deposits. [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4]
- In February 2026 the SFC set out a high-level framework for platforms to offer perpetual contracts (futures with no expiry date). [S:49f642bdee28, Margin arrangements section] It says margin should be cash, or stablecoins or tokenised deposits regulated by the HKMA. [S:49f642bdee28, Margin arrangements section]

## Cost and capital drivers

- The HKMA's liquidity guidance lets a bank that must meet the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) treat qualifying tokens it issues as deposits or unsecured funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
- The LCR checks that a bank holds enough easy-to-sell assets to meet cash outflows during a short period of stress. (concept)
- The same guidance says these tokens cannot count as stable retail or small business deposits. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
- If the bank cannot always identify the holders, it must treat the tokens as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
- If tokens mainly serve payments for wholesale clients with an operational relationship, the guidance says the rules for operational deposits should be followed. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4] Operational deposits are cash that clients keep with a bank for day-to-day clearing and cash management. (concept)
- A bank that holds another bank's tokens must treat them like unsecured loans to financial institutions for liquidity purposes. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 5]
- The HKMA's non-binding DLT note puts full responsibility on the board and senior management. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 1-4 and 8] It covers network choice, smart contracts, settlement finality and key security. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 1-4 and 8]
- Settlement finality is the point where a payment can no longer be reversed. (concept)

## Official signals

- The HKMA named seven Tokenised Deposit Banks and 13 other industry pioneers for EnsembleTX. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annexes A-B]
- In October 2025 the HKMA Chief Executive said six banks had launched tokenised deposit services through the Supervisory Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, Supervisory Incubator for DLT section]
- EnsembleTX is to run throughout 2026. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3] Banks settle with each other first through the Hong Kong dollar Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
- The HKMA plans a step-by-step upgrade to round-the-clock settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA plans to add settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] It also plans to run EnsembleTX 24/7 by then. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- The HKMA is to study trade-finance uses of tokenised deposits with the Mainland, with pilot deals to be done by end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 99]
- In June 2026 an HKMA seminar for corporate treasurers drew over 150 people, including staff of about 50 corporates and 30 financial institutions. [S:05369e6084ea, para 1]

## Industry benchmarks

- KPMG China (KPMG), an accounting and advisory firm that sells services to banks, published its Hong Kong Banking Report in 2026. In the report's commentary (an opinion, not a measured figure), it said most digital-asset work is still small beside traditional banking. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, p.38]
- The same 2026 KPMG commentary says many local and regional Hong Kong banks are waiting to see how the market develops. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, p.42] It notes that spending on technology, talent and compliance can look like cost, not value, in the short term. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, p.42]
- No reliable industry figure for tokenised-deposit volumes or fees in Hong Kong was found.

## Analysis

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** Do tokenised deposits earn new money, or mainly protect deposits and payment business the bank already has?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Split the value into three parts: deposit balances kept or won, fees for treasury services, and a role in settling tokenised assets.
> - Set that against build costs, links to other banks, and the liquidity treatment of the tokens.
> - Ask how much of the value is defensive: balances the bank keeps that might otherwise leave, even if the product's own fee income is small.
> **What it depends on:** corporate demand for round-the-clock payments; how many banks connect; whether holders can be identified; the pace of stablecoin use.
> **Official signposts:**
> - Plans for CBDC settlement and 24/7 running of EnsembleTX. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
> - The trade-finance pilot with the Mainland. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 99]
> - The SFC's round-the-clock trading pilot for tokenised products. [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4]
> **What this is not:** not a forecast, not advice and not the regulator's view.
